available_outcomes.name: Venous thromboembolism (VTE)
available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 1. Demographics between the control and TXA treated groups ... Venus thromboembolism % (n) | Control n = 62: 17.7 (11) | TXA n = 53: 13.2 (7) ... Furthermore, the venous thromboembolism (VTE) rate between the two groups was 17.7% (n = 11) for the control group versus 13.2% (n = 7) for the TXA group (p = 0.68).

quotes.confounding: For non-assessed variables, the patients may not necessarily match because although there is a hospital TXA protocol, the TXA was given at the attending surgeon’s discretion, other factors may have determined the need for the TXA.
quotes.selection: In addition, being a tertiary care facility with a large rural catchment area can prohibit some patient’s arriving within our 3 hr administration window and unable to receive TXA, thus were included with the control group.
quotes.classification: After approval from the Institutional Review Board, non-randomized data was abstracted from our hospital trauma registry between 2013 and 2016.
quotes.deviations: All patients received at least a single blood product.
quotes.missingData: Only patients meeting all criteria described above were included in the analysis.
quotes.measurement: Patient arrival at the hospital is determined as Day 0 and all future time points are relative to this point.
quotes.reporting: We tested, if mortality rate among patients receiving full TXA was significantly lower than the mortality rate in the control group (without TXA administration), by using the two proportion z-test.
